run: architecture candidate 6: both readings of a window that cuts a coordination shell on every natural window of the ten dev cases and the Demo (validation/run.js shell-cuts at 39e1c3a), 2026-10-19
evidence: Two rules decide whether a bond window cuts a coordination shell, both kept unchanged by candidate 6 and both now readings of the shell module (src/llm/context/shells.js): the Workbench asks on the CN margin (cnMarginCut: the window overlaps the shell and holds fewer partner atoms by >= max(0.5, 15 % of the shell's CN)), compute_bond_angles refuses on the coordination counts (countsCut: more than half the central atoms unbonded, or fewer than 60 % with the most common count). On 149 natural windows (each closed shell's triplet around the polyhedron's centre in its whole shell, its first peak alone, its top 0.2 A earlier and later, and the Demo's historical Ta-Se windows) they agree on 134 (6 cut by both, 128 by neither). The counts alone refuse 11: dev-offcentre's whole Nb-Nb shell (3.40-4.24 A, CN 5.46, 52 % share the modal 5: its counts spread because the shell runs into the next) and 10 windows with the top 0.2 A early whose CN stays within the margin (the Demo's Ga-Ga 6.88-7.53 A, 11.2 of 11.9 at 52 %; dev-jahn-teller's Cu-K 6.87 of 8 at 38 %; ...). The CN margin alone asks on 4 first peaks whose counts form a sub-shell: the Demo's Ta-Se (3.25 of 6, 72 % have 3), dev-jahn-teller's four short Cu-F (3.98 of 6, 92 % have 4), the Demo's Se-Se (2.78 of 12, 76 %), dev-offcentre's one short Nb-O (0.89 of 6, 72 %). Both cut the spot check's 2.3-2.7 A and the old first-peak window 2.33-2.71 A on the Demo, two first peaks and two early cuts on the dev cases.
proposed_fix: Recommendation, not approved, for the user: compute_bond_angles refuses on the Workbench's CN-margin reading (window().cnMargin.cut) instead of the coordination counts, so one rule decides a cut: a window the Workbench did not question is not refused, and a whole shell never is (dev-offcentre's Nb-Nb). Its effect on the dev windows: the 10 slightly cut windows would run (their CN within 15 % of the shell's; their angles are those of a nearly whole shell), and the 4 sub-shell first peaks would be refused unless the user chose them, which the Workbench's question already asks before the call. The skill's firm rule and its 60 % judgment call (coordination-shells SKILL.md) would change with it, which is the user's text. Until the user decides, both rules stay as they are.
